LESSON: SIGN READING 6.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Sign Reading 6.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 6.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we predict the ending of a story, poem or conversation? 2. How can we tell where events in a story have taken place?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 6.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Speaking and signing skills; as learner summarises the events in the story.

Values:
Respect: Open minded as the learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers as they look at pictures and say as they sign what will happen in the

story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skill: Effective communication as learner answers comprehension questions correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate sign reading skills for comprehension to their learning in Kenya Sign Language Activities
